newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state offers dairy firm to anchor investors.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state offers dairy firm to anchor investors.

text.p: The Egyptian state said on Tuesday it would auction a majority stake in loss-making firm Misr Milk and Food or its factories to one or more anchor investors.
The state-owned Holding Company for Food Industries announced in the official Al-Ahram newspaper investors can buy part or all its 9,866,005 shares in the dairy firm.
The investors could also buy -- or lease -- one or more of the eight factories belonging to Misr Milk.
The holding company said Misr Milk has a paid-up capital of 40 million pounds, divided into 10 million shares. Government agencies hold the shares not owned by the holding firm.

The holding company invited investors to submit bids before noon (1000 gmt) on Monday, March 3, 1997. Bids should be accompanied with a cash or bank guarantee of 2.5 million pounds for the whole firm or 500,000 pounds for each factory.
The firm's unaudited losses in the financial year 1995/96 were 27 million pounds on turnover of 125 million, a source at the holding company told Reuters.
"But the losses went down against the previous year's 40 million on turnover of 124.38 million," he added. The state prices the firm's products.
Investors can call Abdel Sattar Soleiman, head of technical sectors, at 202 349-2312 or fax him at 202 360-4026.
Misr Milk has 10 outlets and a fleet of 352 vehicles.
